green_summary.RunnerInfra.v1: tools/infra/runner.mjs validate|qualify|up|probe|stop. Exit contract 0=PASS 1=input/prerequisite 2=verification failure, matching I01/I03 (registry+refs loads fail-closed, displayPath/redactHostPaths on every structured field, host paths never echoed, no skip/mock anywhere). validate runs the full structural gate over the six domain files (image lock pins/upGate closed, role boundary invariants, worker-unwritable control volumes, authority uniqueness REFUSE rules, compose declaration gate incl. read-only rootfs + cap_drop ALL + no-new-privileges + loopback + internal network + named-volumes-only + docker.sock ban + 1:1 service/role mapping, Dockerfile lock-resolved base + non-root USER) and exits 0 on committed files with catalogGaps reported explicitly (3 refs missing from the I01-owned catalog). qualify evaluates 8 evidence categories on the VERIFIED/RECORDED/UNVERIFIED ladder (6 UNVERIFIED: container-image, role-isolation-enforcement, control-directory-closure, authority-exclusivity, secret-refs-registered, credentials-provisioned; 2 RECORDED: source-pins, role-boundary-declaration), binds sha256 of registry + all six domain files, exits 2 NOT_READY by design. up refuses in stages exactly like outline: UP_REFUSED_RUNNER_LOCK_NOT_READY (2 components without authenticated digests) -> UP_NOT_AUTHORIZED (closed gate) -> UP_REFUSED_CONTAINER_DAEMON_UNREACHABLE (docker EPERM observed, reported verbatim) -> UP_NOT_EXECUTED; infra starts/stops nothing and holds no DAG/phase/job queue.
green_summary.RoleBoundary.v1: infra/delivery/runner/role-policy.json: six roles (controller/author/test-author/reviewer/publisher/isolator), each with a distinct principal label + credential scope (controller=runner-authority, author=worker-author-api, reviewer=worker-review-api; test-author/publisher/isolator honestly UNASSIGNED rather than inventing refs), distinct workspace volumes, readOnlyRootFilesystem=true, capabilities drop ALL, internal-only network. grantedRefs tier rule: a ref resolves only to its single bound role; publisher/isolator-tier refs can never appear in ordinary worker scopes. infra/delivery/runner/workspace-mounts.json: control volumes (comet state/locks, receipts/approval payloads, issuance material) are worker-unwritable and mount for the controller only; worker workspaces are named volumes with no host binds; docker socket forbidden everywhere. infra/delivery/runner/compose.yaml declares all six role services with independent volumes, read-only rootfs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, loopback port (controller only), internal network; images only via ${COMET_RUNNER_IMAGE:?} resolved from the lock. infra/delivery/runner/Dockerfile: build declaration from the pinned source + two SHA256-pinned patches via the qualified tools/comet build contract (P1_1/P1_6, fingerprint cb1151b4...), base image and hashes only via --build-arg from the lock, non-root USER comet; the containerized build step itself is UNVERIFIED on this host (no daemon, EPERM).
green_summary.Authority.v1: infra/delivery/runner/authority-registration.example.json: one fixed authority + workspace, ids deliberately null/UNVERIFIED until a real runner start reads them back; uniqueness block declares and the validator enforces REFUSE for concurrent writers and copied state; at most one registration per (authorityId, workspaceId) — a second registration on the same authority is AUTHORITY_DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION; registrations stays empty until the real Runner exists. probes are real subcommands: probe --case role-denial and --case duplicate-authority exit 2 with structured UNVERIFIED + exact reason + requiredInputs + plannedSteps (per-channel Edit/Shell/MCP negative-write matrix, docker.sock/host-HOME denial, controller-kill phase-pickup rejection, copied-state second-writer refusal, one-writer readback); with --endpoint they genuinely attempt a real request and report the raw failure (EPERM observed in this sandbox) — the same command runs unchanged against a future live runner. stop is honestly UNVERIFIED: this tool never started a stack.
